request.title: fix: harden Effect architecture boundaries
request.description:
## Summary

- Applies the Effect architecture review findings to @effect-agent/core.
- Rejects inconsistent terminal completion metadata at the public Schema boundary, keeps approval errors on the canonical ToolCallId type, and removes ambient runtime access from ID generation.
- Keeps the first package commit isolated to [packages/core](https://github.com/danieljvdm/effect-agent/tree/33490f6b94bf43fdd729660a45ad5a5fb0910d3a/packages/core) so other package reviews can land as separate commits.

## What went wrong

Core documented the exhausted completion invariant but enforced it only at engine construction sites. Decoded events could therefore disagree about whether a budget was exhausted. Approval errors also weakened ToolCallId to a general non-empty string, while the default ID service reached directly into ambient Web Crypto. Together, those choices left public boundaries weaker than the domain types and coupled an inward package to runtime state.

## Architecture

- [Completion event schemas](https://github.com/danieljvdm/effect-agent/blob/33490f6b94bf43fdd729660a45ad5a5fb0910d3a/packages/core/src/events.ts#L143-L267) now own the relationship between finishReason, exhausted, and runDisposition.
- [Approval errors](https://github.com/danieljvdm/effect-agent/blob/33490f6b94bf43fdd729660a45ad5a5fb0910d3a/packages/core/src/errors.ts#L43-L99) decode native Effect AI call IDs once at the core boundary and retain ToolCallId internally.
- [The ID service](https://github.com/danieljvdm/effect-agent/blob/33490f6b94bf43fdd729660a45ad5a5fb0910d3a/packages/core/src/services.ts#L1-L34) delegates entropy to the Effect AI generator, whose Random service remains fiber-local and seedable.

## Evidence

- [Regression coverage](https://github.com/danieljvdm/effect-agent/blob/33490f6b94bf43fdd729660a45ad5a5fb0910d3a/packages/core/test/core.test.ts#L615-L692) exercises valid and invalid terminal event combinations. The core suite passes all 25 tests.

request.title: fix(session): preserve durable run duration deadlines
request.description:
## Summary

- define `maxDuration` as one wall-clock allowance for a logical Run, including process loss, recovery gaps, approvals, unknown-outcome suspension, and `waitingForChild`
- derive one absolute deadline from the first canonical `UserInputRecorded` record and pass it to every replacement Attempt through a tightening-only engine option
- allow only coordinator-proven, already-settled child joins to finish after expiry, then fail the parent typed before another model or ordinary Tool call
- update the runtime/subagent contracts, correct certification fixtures that had relied on the accidental per-Attempt reset, rebuild the Action bundle, and add a patch changeset

## What was wrong

The engine sampled `Clock.currentTimeMillis` whenever `AgentRuntime.stream` was instantiated. The durable coordinator creates a new stream for every Attempt, so a parent resumed after `waitingForChild` received a fresh `maxDuration` allowance.

A deterministic public-seam reproduction through `DurableAgentRuntime.processConversationResolved` demonstrated the defect: after the parent suspended, advancing `TestClock` by 31 seconds and settling the child still let the parent complete. The new RUN-030 regression initially failed with actual `completed` versus expected `failed`.

The architectural contract is wall clock per logical Run—not per Attempt and not cumulative worker-active time. The initial canonical input is the durable Run-start authority, so queue/admission time is excluded while every later suspension and recovery gap is included.

## Implementation

- [Engine deadline seam](packages/engine/src/run-options.ts) and [enforcement](packages/engine/src/index.ts)
- [Durable deadline derivation and settled-child cleanup proof](packages/session/src/durable-runtime.ts)
- [RUN-030 public durable regression](packages/testing/test/durable-subagents.test.ts)
- [Runtime contract](docs/spec/runtime.md) and [subagent suspension contract](docs/spec/subagents.md)
- [Changeset](.changeset/durable-run-duration.md)

The expired-parent path still verifies and commits the canonical child join and releases its reservation before recording the typed duration failure. The test proves one child invocation, one join, a released reservation, no second parent model prompt, and `SubmissionSettled.policyLimit === "duration"`.

## Evidence

Green on latest `main` base:

- `vp test run packages/testing/test/durable-subagents.test.ts -t "RUN-030"` — 1 passed
- `vp test run packages/testing/test/certification-memory.test.ts packages/testing/test/certification-sqlite.test.ts` — 9 passed
- `vp test run packages/testing/test/durable-subagents.test.ts packages/testing/test/durable-runtime.test.ts packages/engine/test/agent-runtime.test.ts` — 153 passed
- `vp run check`
- `vp run build`
- serialized Vite+ package graph: every runtime, storage, process-kill, certification, chaos, and soak suite passed; 28/29 testing files passed (224 tests)
- `vp run --concurrency-limit 1 -F './examples/*' test` — all example suites passed

Local gate note: the exact `vp run ready` wrapper is blocked on this macOS host by Vite+ concurrent spawn error 22. Serialized execution reaches only two unchanged release-workflow shell-fixture timeouts (`toolchain.test.ts`, 15s and 90s); all product/runtime tests pass. The required clean-Linux Static checks, Tests, Build, and `ready` jobs remain mandatory before merge.

Closes #47

request.title: fix(browser-run): hide extraction schema diagnostics
request.description:
## Summary

- Return a fixed `WebCaptureDecodeFailed` message when structured browser extraction does not satisfy the caller's Effect Schema, keeping parse diagnostics out of model context. See the [failure mapping](https://github.com/danieljvdm/effect-agent/blob/0f29ae16aee5c3d1968550363a8320a8efd20a9c/packages/capabilities/src/web-capture.ts#L556-L565).
- Add a full Agent run regression that puts attacker-controlled text in an invalid field and proves the marker is absent from the Tool failure. See the [regression](https://github.com/danieljvdm/effect-agent/blob/0f29ae16aee5c3d1968550363a8320a8efd20a9c/packages/capabilities/test/web-capture.test.ts#L570-L580).
- Ship the correction as a patch change to `@effect-agent/capabilities`.

## What went wrong

`WebCapture.makeExtract` correctly treated structured browser output as untrusted and decoded it through the caller-owned Schema. Its failure handler then interpolated `String(error)` into `WebCaptureFailure.message`. Effect Schema parse errors can include rejected values. Because the Tool uses `failureMode: "return"`, that message becomes model-visible, so page-controlled text could be echoed into the next model turn.

Mapping every decode error to a fixed message closes that channel. The stable `WebCaptureDecodeFailed` tag still tells callers what happened, while raw parse diagnostics no longer cross the Tool boundary.

## Evidence

The three focused browser capture suites pass all 37 tests. The regression sends `secret-token=attacker-controlled` where a number is required and asserts that the serialized Tool result does not contain the marker.

+---
+"@effect-agent/capabilities": patch
+---
+
+Keep structured extraction schema diagnostics out of model-visible WebCapture failures.
